title: What are the tyre strategy options for the Bahrain GP in Malaysia?
excerpt:
It’s taken 16 races but finally an engine not made by Mercedes has powered a driver to pole position in 2026. It was the Red Bull Powertrains/Ford unit bolted to the back of Max Verstappen that did the business at Sepang.

Alongside him on the front row, he has Lewis Hamilton, with Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc just behind… but the sense in Sepang is that Qualifying positions aren’t going to count for very much on race day.

Our Bahraini hosts this weekend have bought a little bit of Sakhir to South East Asia, with illuminated palm trees and shaded couches in the style of the Bahrain International Circuit, but what they’re really bought is the sort of rough asphalt and extreme temperatures we’re used to seeing in the Bahrain Grand Prix. After two races with virtually no tyre degradation, we’re going to see three races’ worth of deg in one afternoon.

title: What the teams said – Qualifying in Malaysia
excerpt:
The drivers and teams report back on all the action from final practice and Qualifying for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit.

Oct 03, 2026 12:53pm UTC

Red Bull

Max Verstappen looked strong on Friday, and he continued that form throughout Saturday to grab his first pole of the season. The second Qualifying began, it never really looked in doubt – the Dutchman fast from the off, as he eventually beat the field by nearly three tenths of a second. It was a dominant performance from Verstappen, but his Red Bull team mate also impressed and backed him up with third. That was Isack Hadjar's joint-best Qualifying result of the season, but he has that five-place grid drop to serve and thus will start eighth tomorrow.

Max Verstappen, 1st, 1:35.130

“It was an incredible result for us and it was a very proud moment. This weekend was positive from FP1 and we have just been trying to improve the car further and keep tweaking it. The Team have been working really hard and made some big steps forward and I think this particular track layout suited our car even more. Tomorrow will be all about tyres, tyres, tyres and how we manage the degradation.

"It’s been quite a long road to this point since we started the year. Everyone has been working so hard to get the car where it was today, so to really be able to put all this hard work into Pole is fantastic. This really means a lot to the Team and I hope everyone is very proud. We have been quite clear that we want to win a race this year, so we’ll try to do that tomorrow."

Isack Hadjar, 3rd, 1:35.558

“Mixed feelings for me today. Obviously, we can be very happy with P1 and P3 and the overall performance of the car, which is now so much better than where I left it before my injury. I feel I got stronger with every lap I drove since FP1, but we were very limited here with the number of laps we could get in each session. If I had managed to get a few more in, even P2 could have been possible today because my last lap was not perfect. Max, though, was simply untouchable in Qualifying.

"On the other hand, it is a shame that I have to take the penalty and start from P8. Otherwise, I would have had the chance to compare myself to two multiple World Champions right from the start at the front, and that would have been fun.

"Now I have to fight the Mercedes, the McLarens and Charles first, which will not be easy, and try to climb through the field. But anything is possible, so I am still aiming for the podium tomorrow."

Laurent Mekies, Team Principal

"A fantastic result for the whole Team today and a special moment as it’s the first Pole position for us as a complete manufacturer with the Red Bull Ford Powertrains. From the start, this has been a project that embodies Red Bull’s disruptive spirit. To take the design and construction of a power unit in-house and deliver a competitive package in just five years was crazy, but Red Bull have made it happen. For a PU manufacturer to come into the sport with its first new design and take a Pole position in its 16th grand prix is a remarkable achievement.

"We’ve had good pace since the start of the weekend, but in Qualifying Max found another level: quickest in every session and almost three tenths clear with his final flying lap. So, congratulations to him for his first Pole position of the season and congratulations to the whole Team. We have been making strong steps since the summer break, getting closer and closer on absolute pace and scoring podiums on a regular basis. This Pole is a testimony to all of the hard work that everyone at track and at the factory is doing to close the gap. It was a fantastic performance from Isack too. Fast all weekend, P3 in the session and missing out the first row by just a little more than a tenth. Of course, it’s a shame that he has to take a grid penalty tomorrow, but it’s also clear that he has the pace to fight his way forward.

"The race is going to be a whole new challenge. It will undoubtedly be dominated by tyre management and the punishing conditions here in Sepang. So we reset tonight and concentrate on getting the most of our car for the brutal conditions expected tomorrow. Isack and Max have been working hard with the Team to understand the tyres here and I am sure they will put on a strong fight in the middle of a very tight field at the front."

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Pole position qualifier Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red Bull Racing celebrates in parc ferme during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Third placed qualifier Isack Hadjar of France and Oracle Red Bull Racing looks on during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Mario Renzi - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Ferrari

Ferrari looked to be the third-fastest team in final practice, but their car came alive in Qualifying. For starters, they made it through Q1 on the mediums, putting them on a different tyre strategy for tomorrow compared to their rivals. With both easily making Q3, the two Scuderia drivers looked evenly matched, but it was Lewis Hamilton whose superior knowledge of this place paid dividends. With five previous poles here, he came the closest to grabbing a sixth, but just did not have the pace to fight with Verstappen.

Charles Leclerc inherits a place thanks to grid drops, and is the only driver in the entire field to have run the hard tyre in Sepang, so has valuable knowledge for tomorrow’s Grand Prix with regards the C2 compound.

Lewis Hamilton, 2nd, 1:35.428

"First of all, a huge thank you to everyone in the team. The conditions have been incredibly demanding all weekend, not just for the drivers but also for the mechanics and engineers, and they’ve done a fantastic job. We worked hard session after session to understand the car and find the right balance in these temperatures, and the adjustments we made ahead of qualifying definitely helped us take a step forward. We managed to put it all together when it mattered most. Tomorrow will be a very different challenge, with tyre management likely to play a big part, but it’s great to be starting on the front row. Now we just need to focus on executing a clean race, maximising every opportunity and seeing what we can achieve."

Charles Leclerc, 5th, 1:35.666

"P4 is not a bad place to start from. At the same time, it wasn't a great qualifying, particularly in Q3. I tried my best, but from sector two onwards, I was sliding around with the rear, probably being a bit too aggressive with the setup. That’s the way it goes sometimes. Tyre management and strategy will both be key in the race. Let’s see what we can bring home for the team."

Fred Vasseur, Team Principal

"Today’s qualifying went well for us and I am happy to have both cars starting on the first and second rows with Lewis and Charles. I want to thank everyone both at the track and in Maranello for the great work they have done.

"Lewis produced a really strong lap and it’s a shame for Charles that he wasn't able to put everything together on his final attempt, because he had the pace to set a time very close to Lewis’. But it’s tomorrow that counts. We know that the main factors in the race will be degradation, pace and tyre management in general. These elements will be more important than our grid positions. It will be a long race tomorrow and there is everything to play for."

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Pole position qualifier Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red Bull Racing and Second placed qualifier Lewis Hamilton of Great Britain and Scuderia Ferrari congratulate each other in parc ferme during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Charles Leclerc of Monaco driving the (16) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 in the Pitlane during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

Mercedes

Mercedes made a step forward in FP3, so much so they looked right in the mix for pole. But when Qualifying began, George Russell was off the pace from word go. Kimi Antonelli looked quicker, but he ran wide on his first lap in Q2 and lost the time to track limits, forcing him into using a second set of tyres. That cost the Italian, who only had one set for Q3. He came out midway through the segment by himself and managed to grab fourth, which becomes P3 when Hadjar’s penalty is applied.

But Russell could only manage eighth, and while he also gains a place thanks to Hadjar’s drop, seventh is hardly what he needed as he tries to keep the momentum from Baku going.

Kimi Antonelli, 4th, 1:35.631

"We were strong in FP3, so it was a shame that we dropped back in terms of competitiveness come qualifying. It is a unique circuit here with a very aggressive tarmac and in incredibly hot conditions; that makes it difficult to deliver the same performance consistently. We will go around the loop tonight to see what we could have done differently and to make sure we understand exactly where we went wrong.

"I put myself under quite a lot of pressure with only one new set of Soft tyres in Q3 but I did what I could. If we had a second set, I think we could have fought for the front-row, but I don't think we could have challenged Max (Verstappen) for pole. He has looked like the quickest car all weekend and so it proved today.

"P3 is not a bad place to be starting from all things considered. The tyre degradation is likely to be very high and, in all probability, it will be a multi-stop race. That will hopefully open up opportunities for us if we have good race pace. There is still the possibility of rain too which could make things even more exciting so I'm looking forward to tomorrow."

George Russell, 8th, 1:35.871

"We've struggled today and that is reflected by what was our toughest Saturday of the year. It is so hot here and the tarmac is very aggressive, with the low grip making lap times several seconds slower than when we last raced here in 2017. That may have impacted our performance comparatively to what we have seen at other circuits, but it is true to say that we have clearly suffered more than our closest competitors this weekend. We didn't expect to struggle this much here in Malaysia, and we will work hard to understand why.

"Whilst we are frustrated by our performance today, tomorrow will be a very different challenge. The race is likely to be dominated by high tyre degradation and keeping the tyres in good shape across a full stint will be the key to a good Grand Prix. Whilst we have ground to make up, we know it should be possible to overtake if you have the speed so we will be giving it our all to make up ground."

Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport

"That was our toughest Saturday of the season, and we need to dig deep to understand exactly why that was. We have plenty to analyse from the two days of running here in Sepang to get to the heart of why we have struggled so much. There are many factors we will need to take into consideration, and we can't rule anything out at this stage.

"Tomorrow is another day. With the levels of degradation we saw in practice, we are heading a little bit into the unknown in terms of both race pace and strategy. It will likely be a Grand Prix where we see multiple stops for each car and that could provide opportunities. Equally, we know that our race pace on Friday wasn't the strongest, so we hope the changes we have made to the car since then have helped with that, even if they didn't benefit us on our single laps today."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"Today was clearly a disappointing result relative to our expectations coming into the weekend. We showed encouraging pace in FP3, but couldn't extract the same performance when we needed come qualifying. We will spend time this evening, and in the coming days, analysing the data to understand why we fell away compared to our competitors and what lessons we can take forward.

"The focus now turns to tomorrow. This circuit is placing huge demands on the tyres and degradation is expected to be very high, which means strategy, tyre management and operational execution will all be critical. Whilst we would have preferred to be starting further forward, both drivers are in positions where they can fight for solid results. With a race that looks likely to feature multiple pit stops and plenty of strategic variation, there will be opportunities to make progress if we have decent pace."

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images)

McLaren

McLaren’s form remained a little unknown heading into Qualifying, with Lando Norris looking fast at times and Oscar Piastri a shade behind, but the duo throwing in a few mistakes along the way. But over one-lap when it mattered, both impressed and made Q3 comfortably. Piastri had the edge in Q1, Q2 and their first runs in Q3, but when it mattered, Norris dived ahead to the tune of just 0.005s. In the end, they did not have the pace to fight with the cars ahead, but they at least will start in front of Russell and Hadjar as the team targets a decent haul of points to try and fight Ferrari for P2 in the Championship.

Lando Norris, 6th, 1:35.757

“I'm pretty satisfied with my final lap. I feel I put it all together and did a good job with what we had. However, it's clear we are a long way off the pace. My car is struggling with speed on the straights, and we've lacked general pace all weekend, so starting fifth is not a surprise. We don't expect any miracles, and it’s obvious the Red Bulls are in a class of their own here.

“Tomorrow will be a very different and challenging race for everyone. The tyre degradation is higher than we've seen all year, which will likely force a two or three-stop strategy. This could create opportunities with Safety Cars and varying strategies. It’s going to be a tough, physical race where managing the car lap after lap will be crucial. While we're not where we want to be in terms of performance, the unpredictable nature of this race could be a good thing for us, and we'll be ready to seize any chances that come our way.”

Oscar Piastri, 7th, 1:35.762

“That’s Qualifying done. A P7 result, but starting P6 tomorrow due to a penalty ahead. Overall, it was a decent session, but we’re still struggling for pace. I just didn’t get the best final lap, and had no grip at Turn Two, meaning we weren’t able to get the last bit of performance out of the car.

“Looking ahead, it is going to be a long and tough one tomorrow. Our long-run pace looked pretty good yesterday, but the competitors around us didn’t look bad either, so it may be tricky to move forward, but we will do what we can to maximise strategy and any overtaking potential here. Let’s see what’s possible.”

Andrea Stella, Team Principal

“It wasn’t an easy Qualifying session on a track that presents so many technical and physical challenges, given the very high temperatures and the highest tarmac roughness of the season, both for the drivers and the teams. Today’s result comes as no surprise. We’d already seen last week that Red Bull had taken a significant step forward, and today that was even more evident. For our part, we know there’s work to be done to maximise the car’s potential, but, in any case, we’ve achieved a result that means we’ll be in contention in tomorrow’s race, which is important in its own right.

“Both Lando and Oscar did a good job on a circuit they’d never driven before. As was the case in Baku, Lando’s car continued to suffer from a speed deficit on the straights, and we need to keep analysing the causes of this together with our partners at HPP.

“Whether the track is wet or dry, we’re expecting a race full of twists and turns. Tyre degradation will be a key factor for everyone and, based on what we saw in free practice, we believe we’re in a good position. It’ll be a tight race, and our aim is clear: to capitalise on every opportunity that arises and fight for a place on the podium.”

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Lando Norris of Great Britain driving the (1) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Oscar Piastri of Australia driving the (81) McLaren MCL40 Mercedes in the Pitlane during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images)

Alpine

With Franco Colapinto’s grid penalties looming, the team opted to use the Argentine to help Pierre Gasly out. It seemed to work well, with the Frenchman making Q3 with relative ease. Once there, Gasly only had one fresh set of soft tyres but put those to good effect to beat midfield rival Gabriel Bortoleto to ninth. On a day where the big four teams looked solid, P9 is a strong result for Gasly who is chasing points with Alpine still locked in a tight fight for P5 in the Teams’ Championship.

Pierre Gasly, 9th, 1:37.210

“The car has been competitive again today and we reached our target of being in Q3, so I am happy we achieved that. We knew P9 was probably the best we could realistically do, so we decided to use two used sets of Softs in Q3 and save a set of new Softs for tomorrow in case they are needed. With Gabriel [Bortoleto] in Q3, we just needed to be ahead of him, which we managed. I am pleased with the car at the moment, it's in a comfortable place, quick enough for Q3 regularly as we have seen at the last couple of races, and we just have to keep working hard as the gap to those ahead is still just too far. It's a very fun track to drive, fast and flowing and I am sure it will bring some big challenges tomorrow. We know the target tomorrow is to translate this performance into points, and I am sure we will see different strategies up and down the field so we will need to stay focused and ready to adapt to anything which might spring up in the race.”

Franco Colapinto, 15th, No time set in Q2

“It's been an unconventional Qualifying day and weekend for us, knowing the grid penalties we'll have applied tomorrow. We did not really have a proper go at it, but we knew that would be the case and the focus has been on high fuel running and getting the most from the car and the tyres during the race. Free Practice 3 was really the first time we ran with low fuel and the car has felt strong in all conditions, which is positive and again shows we've made progress with recent upgrades we've brought to the car. We've saved some new tyres for tomorrow's Grand Prix, giving us some more flexibility and strategy options, which we hope to benefit from. Hopefully the work we've put in on set-up can help with that and hopefully we can have some fun during the race and make some moves. Overall, it was a well-managed Qualifying by the team with Pierre also in Q3, so hopefully we can score some strong points for the team.”

Steve Nielsen, Managing Director

“That was probably as good as it was going to get for us today and Qualifying very much played out to our expectations. Pierre did another solid job to put the car in Q3 where, given the pace we had, he did not need to take any risks but just needed clean, fast laps to be comfortably ahead of some of our midfield rivals. We ran two used sets of Softs in Q3 as we knew P9 was probably the best we could have achieved with the top four teams clearly ahead this weekend. That means we have some flexibility and options on strategy for tomorrow where we all head into the unknown on what to expect with the tyres and the varying conditions. On Franco's side, he has driven well today and we had some flexibility on how his Qualifying progressed, knowing he has the grid penalty for tomorrow. We had the option for him to give Pierre a tow but we realised the performance gain was fairly low and too much of a risk. We also wanted to save a new set of Softs for him so we ran a used set in Q2 with an attempt to beat some cars ahead but that came to no avail given the performance difference between a new and a used set. We head into tomorrow's race with some decent options and a clear objective: to score as many points as possible and finish ahead of our rivals in the Championship.”

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Franco Colapinto of Argentina driving the (43) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes leads Lance Stroll of Canada driving the (18) Aston Martin F1 Team AMR26 Honda and Pierre Gasly of France driving the (10) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Pierre Gasly of France driving the (10) Alpine F1 A526 Mercedes on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)

Audi

It was a mixed bag for Audi in Sepang, with the team operating a different strategy to their rivals. They went out on the mediums for their first run in Q1 to save softs, but both needed to run again. Gabriel Bortoleto’s soft-shod lap was good enough to progress, but Nico Hulkenberg’s was not after a lock-up put him wide over the kerbs. The Brazilian then went one better and made it to Q3 for the first time since Zandvoort, and is right in the mix for points tomorrow.

Nico Hulkenberg, 17th, 1:37.970

"It was a disappointing end to Qualifying because the lap was coming together well until the lock-up in the final sector. The margins are so tight these days that you need to get every corner right, and unfortunately that cost us a significant amount of lap time.

"Tomorrow will be a demanding race with high tyre degradation, and the weather could add another element. Starting further back is never ideal, but there are plenty of variables here, so we'll give it our best shot and try to make our way forward."

Gabriel Bortoleto, 10th, 1:37.673

“I’m very happy, I think it was a mega lap – overall, all the laps in Qualifying were very good and I felt really at ease with the car.

“After a tough weekend in Baku, I think this is a very strong response, and it shows the quality of the upgrades package we brought. The whole midfield has closed the gap now, so hats off to the team for the incredible job they’ve done, putting the car in the right window and giving us the confidence to push. If I was able to deliver this today, it’s thanks to them, and I really appreciate that.

“There’s going to be a lot of degradation tomorrow, but that’s the same for everyone. Hopefully we can put together a good race, keep the tyres alive and go for the points.”

Allan McNish, Racing Director

“I think it is fair to say it has been quite a challenging weekend for everybody: coming to a new circuit, getting up to speed and finding the right car balance and feeling has not been easy in these conditions. For us, it all came together in qualifying, where I think we extracted the best performance from the car. The new package was working very well, and Gabi delivered some absolutely fantastic laps throughout the session to get into Q3 and secure a good starting position for tomorrow.

“Nico was on exactly the same pace but unfortunately locked up into Turn 14 on his final lap: he will start 15th after the penalties to Colapinto and Lindblad are applied. Knowing the race pace he has shown, and how well he can fight his way through, I think we have two cars very much in the game tomorrow.”

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Gabriel Bortoleto of Brazil driving the (5) Audi F1 Team R26 on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Peter Fox/Getty Images)

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Seventeenth placed qualifier Nico Hulkenberg of Germany and Audi F1 Team walks in the Pitlane after being eliminated during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

Racing Bulls

Arvid Lindblad had that grid drop coming into Qualifying, and thus ran a different programme to his Racing Bulls team mate. His aim was to make Q2 and then offer Liam Lawson a tow, with the margins in the midfield looking incredibly tight. He did just that, but even with the tow Lawson fell just short of Q3. He was pipped by Bortoleto, but at least stayed ahead of the lead Aston Martin. From P11, Lawson can fight for points – which he needs to, as rival Gasly starts from ninth.

Arvid Lindblad, 16th, No time set in Q2

"I’m reasonably happy with today’s Qualifying. We can see the pace is definitely there, which is a positive. Starting from the back in tomorrow’s race is going to be exciting, there are likely to be plenty of surprises and opportunities, which I’m looking forward to. Most of my running this weekend has been focused on the long runs, so I feel pretty well prepared. There’s likely to be a mixture of two- and three-stop strategies, which should make for an interesting race.”

Liam Lawson, 11th, 1:37.023

"After a comfortable FP3 this morning, it felt like quite a frustrating Qualifying. The car had been competitive so far this weekend, so we'll be reviewing where we lost so much pace. We struggled more with tyres during this session, so management tomorrow is going to be key with the high track temperatures. That being said, there's opportunity for overtaking here, so we'll take our learnings and focus on pulling everything together for the race."

Mattia Spini, Head of Trackside Engineering

“We were missing some pace in Qualifying today after a promising FP3. Given Arvid’s Power Unit penalty, we opted for an unconventional run plan, with the objective to get him into Q2, where he could help Liam with a tow. Despite having to abort his lap in Q1, he was showing good pace, which was encouraging.

“Liam struggled slightly with overall grip and confidence, and unfortunately his fastest lap was not quite enough to reach Q3 today. We appeared to lose some competitiveness relative to FP3, which we now need to take a look at and understand.

“Liam will start tomorrow’s race from P11, just outside the points. Overtaking is possible here, so whoever can manage tyre degradation, while maintaining the strongest pace will finish ahead. With Arvid starting from the back of the grid, we will explore every strategic opportunity to help him gain positions and achieve the result his pace deserves.”

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Liam Lawson of New Zealand and Visa Cash App Racing Bulls prepares to drive in the garage during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Arvid Lindblad of Great Britain driving the (41) Visa Cash App Racing Bulls VCARB 03 RB Ford on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Aston Martin

Fernando Alonso has a strong record here, with five podiums at this track. He seems to really gel with the circuit and it was no different in Qualifying, with the Spaniard making it to Q2 for just the second time this season. Lance Stroll followed him through, the first time Aston Martin have managed to get both cars out of Q1 this year. Given that stat, it is no surprise both recorded their best starting slots of the year, in 12th and 14th.

Fernando Alonso, 12th, 1:37.220

“It was our best Qualifying so far this season and we were about 1.5 seconds from the front in Q2 which is the closest we've been all year. The car is the same as previous races and it's clear we lack performance on the straights, but we do seem to be better suited to this track. Tyre management will be a big factor tomorrow, so let's try have some fun and see what we can do in the race.”

Lance Stroll, 14th, 1:37.566

“We made it through to Q2 and qualified in P14. That’s our most competitive result of this year so far. It clicked for me during the second push lap in Q1 and came together much better. I felt more comfortable in the car during Qualifying than in the practice sessions, although there were some mistakes in Q2 and I think we could’ve gotten slightly more out of it. But we will see what tomorrow brings. I didn’t do many long runs on Friday and it will be tricky conditions with the hot temperatures, the track surface and the tyre degradation.”

Mike Krack, Chief Trackside Officer

“A positive result today, with Fernando in P12 and Lance in P14. Both cars made it into Q2, giving us our best qualifying performance of the year. We’ve enjoyed coming to Sepang, and the low-grip conditions seem to have slightly changed the pecking order, allowing us to be more competitive from the start of practice yesterday. Tomorrow will be a tough challenge, with the hot conditions and a high possibility of rain showers late in the afternoon. We need to stay focused, execute well and maximise every opportunity that comes our way.”

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Fernando Alonso of Spain driving the (14) Aston Martin F1 Team AMR26 Honda on track during final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Peter Fox/Getty Images)

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Lance Stroll of Canada driving the (18) Aston Martin F1 Team AMR26 Honda in the Pitlane during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images)

Williams

Williams looked to be struggling for pace in Malaysia despite their new upgrades, but Carlos Sainz put in a storming last lap in Q1 to progress onwards. His team mate could not follow, Alex Albon qualifying a lowly 20th – although that becomes P18 when Colapinto and Lindblad drop down. Sainz then repeated the trick in Q2 to grab 13th, arguably out-qualifying where the car should have been. But of concern for the team is the fact that the upgrades do not seem to have leapt them as far up the order as perhaps was hoped.

Carlos Sainz, 13th, 1:37.527

title: How Aston Martin 'miracle' earned P12 and P14 for Bahrain GP

title: Hamilton on how Ferrari ‘hit the sweet spot’ in Malaysia
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has praised Ferrari for finding “the sweet spot” in Qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, with the Briton set to start on the front row alongside polesitter Max Verstappen.

This weekend marks F1’s first visit to the Sepang International Circuit since 2017, so there were plenty of unknowns heading into the session, especially as the three hours of practice had seen Red Bull, Ferrari and Mercedes all top the times.

That meant that it was all to play for in Qualifying, but Hamilton didn’t initially seem to be in the mix as he had finished behind Charles Leclerc in the preceding sessions, leaving him pleasantly surprised when his final lap in Q3 earned him P2 on the grid.

He had the slim advantage of having raced in Malaysia before and was elated to produce such a strong result on his return, as he explained: “I think this is the biggest crowd we’ve ever seen here, at least in my time of driving, so I love this energy. A big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us.

“It's so hot here, I keep saying it, but that's made it a massive challenge for the tyres, for the car, for the mechanics in the garage, and I'm really, really thankful to my team.

“We've made so many changes through all these practice sessions and, because the cars are sliding, these tyres are overheating, it was really, really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into Qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot.

“To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max, who's been so quick all weekend, is great and, yeah, I'm so, so grateful.”

Despite Ferrari’s successful efforts to eke out more performance as the weekend progressed, Hamilton noted that any improvements won’t necessarily help them in the Grand Prix, especially as tyre degradation is set to play a significant role.

“I'm much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame,” he said. “Making these tyres last around this track... I mean, they're overheating from the get-go, so every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have, depending on the wind, makes a difference of how far you're going to go.

“But I like to think we've got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I'll just try my best to hold on to it tomorrow.”

After setting the fastest time in FP2, his team mate Leclerc settled for P5 in Qualifying, but is set to gain a position once Isack Hadjar’s five-place grid penalty for taking a new engine is imposed.

While the Monegasque cut a more frustrated figure than Hamilton as balance issues impacted his lap times in Q3, he was optimistic that he would be able to challenge some of their frontrunning rivals in the race.

“I started losing some performance from Q2, particularly when I started pushing the car,” Leclerc said. “The rear started to struggle a little bit more and getting into Q3, that was too much so I was a little bit overbalanced for Q3.

“All in all, it hasn’t been a bad Qualifying. I think Lewis did a super lap and probably didn’t leave much on the table. On my side, it’s P4 tomorrow. It’s all to fight for with the guys in front. It should be an interesting race.

“We are relatively close to the guys in front. Mercedes seemed to be extremely strong yesterday and also this morning. Today in Qualifying [they were] maybe a bit less strong compared to what we expected, so I expect them to be back to where they normally are in the race. If so, it’s going to be difficult to beat them.”

excerpt:
Max Verstappen will start Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia from pole position with Lewis Hamilton alongside him in second, setting up an exciting battle for Sunday's race.

It has also produced the possibility of a repeat of the battle that we saw last time F1 ventured to Sepang in 2017.

Verstappen topped qualifying for Red Bull on Saturday, continuing the sharp uptick in form that followed the team's double podium in Baku last time out.

Hamilton took second on the road following a late improvement to consolidate a front row for Ferrari, in a season that has had its ups and downs for the Scuderia.

It is a near-perfect mirror of 2017, when Verstappen qualified third for Red Bull but powered past Hamilton's Mercedes on lap four to win, while the seven-time champion settled for second after leading from pole.

That race was also notable for Kimi Raikkonen, who qualified second for Ferrari but failed even to start after a turbocharger and inlet manifold duct problem struck on his way to the grid.

Nine years on, there is a Kimi in the top three once again, only this time it is Antonelli rather than Raikkonen.

The Mercedes driver qualified fourth after a mistake in Q2 cost him an extra set of soft tyres and left him short on new rubber for his final run in Q3, but a grid penalty for Red Bull's Isack Hadjar is set to promote him into third place on the starting grid.

What happened nine years ago?

That 2017 victory was only the second of Verstappen's career, occurring one day after his 20th birthday in a season that had been ravaged by reliability woes.

He made his move on Hamilton early, having clocked that the Mercedes was struggling for traction out of the corners. The decisive pass came into Turn 1, where Verstappen was helped by DRS and careful management of his energy deployment, while Hamilton was dealing with power unit de-rating after running down his battery charge defending in the opening laps.

Hamilton chose not to fight hard for the inside line, wary of the risk of contact given his focus on the title battle with Sebastian Vettel.

Once through, Verstappen immediately showed stronger race pace, pulling away from Hamilton and extending his lead through the single pit-stop phase to control the margin comfortably to the flag.

"In the beginning the car felt good and I saw Lewis was struggling a bit with traction... Then once I got past Lewis I could just control my own race,” Verstappen said afterwards.

“The car was very good. If I needed to speed up I sped up. Yeah, it's amazing. It's a very tough race but of course incredible to win,"

Hamilton, who had started from pole, was magnanimous in defeat, conceding that Mercedes simply didn't have the pace to resist Red Bull that weekend.

"A big congratulations to Max and a happy birthday. He did a fantastic job today... The race was a tough one.

“Obviously they just had the upper hand on us today... I feel good, but I think we have some work to do with the car. Obviously we didn't have the pace today, this weekend, so there's still work to do," Hamilton said.

Over the radio, Red Bull boss Christian Horner couldn't contain his delight, telling his driver: "Super, super job Max. Welcome to being a 20-year-old. Great start to a new decade for you, well done."

Verstappen's 20s would continue to bring success as, over the following eight years, he added a further 69 race wins to his achievements, as well as four world championships.

title: Oliver Bearman details shocking Haas issue behind Malaysia struggles
excerpt:
Oliver Bearman has revealed that an unusual error with his car setup on Friday in Malaysia had a direct consequence for his early exit from qualifying.

Bearman ended Saturday's session in 18th place, suffering a Q1 exit alongside his Haas team-mate Esteban Ocon.

The 21-year-old highlighted that he felt underprepared for the session due to a calamitous setup mistake for FP2, which saw the team make incorrect tunings to Bearman's car.

As a result, it put his preparations for qualifying on the back foot as he drove around the circuit with settings that were far from suited to the layout.

"For me, the issue has been an all-weekend-long one," Bearman told media including RacingNews365.

"We started out in FP1, it was okay, but then in FP2 we had a problem with the car setup.

"Basically, the setup that we intended to put on the car was not the setup that ended up on the car, and the car ended up in a state that we would never intend to ever run a race car.

"Not even on an oval would run this type of setup, and basically, from the first lap I did in FP2 I told them, 'Guys, something's wrong with this car'.

"When every lap you do on the same set of tyres is one second off, if you lose two important laps, that's almost half of your laps done in a day.

"So I missed out on FP2, almost, it feels like we learned nothing.

"That really stopped us from getting through into Q2 today."

[Article continues below]

The issue was rectified for the final practice outing on Saturday in Sepang, a session that saw Bearman finish 17th.

Although he felt happier with the car, Bearman stated he was a day late with his preparations compared to his rivals, putting him at a disadvantage for qualifying.

"In FP3, I had two push laps, and I was just trying to learn and figure out what the car needs because everybody else got to do that yesterday,” he said.

"I was learning on the job, and the only time I've actually had a good car and had a good feeling was in that final run.”

While it marked a frustrating turn of events for Bearman, he refused to pin blame on any individual within the team.

"It's no specific person's fault, it's just processes missed and things like that,” Bearman added.

"Everything is always a rush. It's always last minute when we decide what to do.

"What we thought we were running, we were not running at all. It's part of life, but it's a big kick for everybody to make sure that we're on it because without that, I'm in Q2."

title: Lando Norris voices 'hurt' over major McLaren weakness in Malaysia
excerpt:
Lando Norris has stated that his qualifying effort in Malaysia "hurts" as he felt helpless en route to his disappointing result.

Norris ended the day in sixth place, one position ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri.

It marked a difficult showing for the Woking-based squad, who appeared to be the slowest of the top four teams on Saturday.

Norris pinpointed his struggles in a straight line as the major shortcoming on Saturday, insisting his input behind the wheel felt strong.

"I need to see the laps, I need to see what the good things or bad things from each lap were," he told media including RacingNews365

"Obviously, there's always a little bit in it as drivers, but I felt like my lap was very strong.

"It's tough, I'm still struggling a lot in the straights everywhere. I'm just down on every single straight.

"Every time I get a good exit, I'm just slow at the end of the straight, and it just hurts seeing this every single time."

Norris downplays race-day chances

Around the midpoint of the season, McLaren enjoyed a step forward in pace, with Norris bagging three pole positions in four races.

He even climbed to the top step of the podium in Hungary and the Netherlands.

But as he expects the straight-line struggles to carry over to Sunday, Norris is not expecting a competitive showing this time around.

"So I should be higher up, not because I could have done a better job necessarily, but just because we're not getting everything out of the car that we need to.

"That doesn't make my life tough [just] today, but it also makes it tough for tomorrow."

title: George Russell facing 'big question mark' after 'very bad' Mercedes qualifying
excerpt:
George Russell believes "a big question mark" hangs over the merits of Mercedes' major upgrade for this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia after he suffered his worst qualifying performance of the season.

Russell could only finish eighth-quickest in a heavily updated W17, three-quarters of a second adrift of polesitter Max Verstappen in his Red Bull, and a quarter of a second behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who starts fourth.

It is only the second team this season Mercedes has failed to make the top three in qualifying, and for Russell, in particular, after dominating last weekend's grand prix in Azerbaijan, he was left scratching his head over the difference in performance.

Asked whether he knew why it had so far been a more difficult weekend than anticipated, he said: "No, to be honest.

"Obviously, this circuit is a bit of an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the Tarmac. The lap times seven years ago were about six or seven seconds faster, and at certain points on the track, it feels like you're driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone.

"However, it's clearly affecting us more than others."

In terms of trying to understand the upgrade and extract its full potential, and how much remains a learning process, he added: "That is the big question mark.

"If you could have done a direct back-to-back, it would have been great to know. But that's the challenge of this sport.

"If we'd put the upgrade package on last week, even if it was worse, we probably still would have been on pole, and we'd have been saying it was fantastic.

"Equally, if we'd had the old car here, maybe the result would have been even worse. So that's the challenge.

"As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season, and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us."

[Article continues below]

Russell - There's going to be a lot happening

Russell, who goes into the race 66 points adrift of Antonelli in the drivers' standings, stated the numbers from the wind tunnel had indicated "an improvement" with the car, albeit recognising it is the stopwatch at the track that ultimately counts.

"Obviously, as a sport, we need to follow the lap times and not what the numbers say," he said. "The numbers look absolutely fine and in line with expectations. However, the result wasn't."

As to the race, particularly around a circuit where tyre degradation will be high, Russell, who will start seventh with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar serving a five-place penalty after qualifying third, said: "I think there's going to be a lot happening tomorrow.

"The tyre deg is huge, and race pace will be king. So, even though today was a real disappointment, it's not the be-all, end-all."

title: Toto Wolff reveals 'something else going on' after rare qualifying failure
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has admitted Mercedes has been left confused by its lack of pace during qualifying at the Malaysian Grand Prix.

The Brackley-based squad brought a substantial upgrade package to the event as it looked to consolidate its end-of-season push towards double title success.

While Kimi Antonelli was just able to scrape inside the top four, team-mate George Russell had a more difficult time of things in eighth.

The result comes despite Antonelli showing ominous pace in FP3 to lead the pack heading into the qualifying showdown.

“Very difficult to understand,” Wolff told Sky F1.

“We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we didn’t see all year, but then you can say it’s very hot and the tarmac is very different to all the other tracks.

“It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding.

“And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance."

[Article continues below]

Toto Wolff explains lack of pace

The result is just the second time this year that Mercedes has failed to get a car inside the top three.

When asked ot explained where it was losing performance, Wolff added: “It looks like we are very draggy because it's the first time that we're losing a lot of time on the straights, especially to Max.

“And then through the low speed, in Turn 2, we are not able to turn the car, there's just too much understeer.

“Overall, it's things we haven't seen all year.

“Something else is going on. Something else is going on, and we have to understand.

“This is now working through the data and putting our heads together because we still believe that the upgrade works. We just need to understand why not here.”

title: Max Verstappen hails 'pretty incredible' Red Bull surge after scoring season first
excerpt:
Max Verstappen described his first pole position of the season as "pretty incredible" after landing the top spot on the grid for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Verstappen was imperious throughout qualifying at the Sepang International Circuit, finishing fastest in all three sessions, with pole secured by three tenths of a second ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, with a lap of one minute 35.130s.

It is the first non-Mercedes-powered pole of the season, and the first for Verstappen and Red Bull since the curtain-closing race in Abu Dhabi last season.

"It's fantastic," said four-time F1 champion Verstappen on his pole. "We've been trying to get pole, sometimes a bit closer than others, but to finally get it from where we started this season is pretty incredible.

"Looking at the season, how it started for us, and the progression that we have made at some tracks, we were kind of close, but now I think this weekend it was very positive for us.

"From FP1, we started quite well, and from then onwards, we've just been trying to improve the car further, and it's incredible. Honestly, I'm very happy to be on pole here."

As to the possibility of winning the race and ending that additional drought that also goes back to Abu Dhabi, he added: "I'm happy with today, and for sure, I'm going to try to win tomorrow. When you start first, that's the target."

Regarding the challenges he will be facing, he added: "It's very hot, for ourselves, the cars, the brakes, the tyres, so the race is definitely going to be a tough one. You have to manage a lot.

"It's impossible to know at the moment who can do that the best, but at the same time, there is a start where a lot of things can happen, so we just need to be aware, ready, and then we'll see how competitive we are in the race.

"But so far this weekend, I've felt good, confident, and I hope we can show that again tomorrow."

title: Lewis Hamilton reveals late change hit Ferrari 'sweet spot' in Sepang turnaround
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton felt Ferrari "hit the sweet spot" with one final change to his car before qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Hamilton will line up alongside Max Verstappen on the front row of the grid at the Sepang International Circuit, having been beaten by three-tenths of a second.

The seven-time F1 drivers' champion described the litany of tweaks and set-up alterations the Scuderia made on his SF-26 across the weekend, with those changes ultimately coming good when it mattered.

"It's so hot here. I keep saying it, but that's made it a massive challenge for the tyres, for the car, for the mechanics in the garage, and I'm really, really thankful to my team," Hamilton said after the grid-setting session.

"We made so many changes through all these practice sessions, and because the cars are sliding, and these tyres are overheating, it was really, really hard to find a good balance."

Hamilton revealed that one final change to his car paved the way for him to join his old adversary on the front row for the first time since the Hungarian Grand Prix in 2023.

"We made one last change going into qualifying, and I think we hit the sweet spot," the 106-time grand prix winner added.

"So to be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max, who's been so quick all weekend, is great. I'm so, so grateful."

Max Verstappen has taken pole position for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, his first of the 2026 F1 campaign.

Red Bull has looked competitive throughout the race weekend in Sepang and frequently threatened the top of the timesheets.

But when it came to the all-important qualifying laps, it was Verstappen who set the fastest effort of the weekend, clocking a 1:35.130.

The four-time champion improved by one-tenth on his final attempt, however his first effort would have been enough to seal the deal.

Amid a series of improvements in the final trips around the circuit, Lewis Hamilton fired himself up to second place.

Red Bull's strong pace was backed up by an impressive run for Isack Hadjar, who set the third-fastest lap.

title: Aston Martin cause major shock in Sepang qualifying
excerpt:
Aston Martin caused a major shock in qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

In what has been a torrid campaign for the team so far this season, only once in the previous 15 race weekends had one of its cars made the second session of qualifying for a grand prix.

title: Red Bull branded 'biggest threat' to Mercedes as F1 recovery gathers pace
excerpt:
Anthony Davidson has declared that Red Bull is fast becoming the "biggest threat" to Mercedes in F1, after the team locked out second and third places behind Kimi Antonelli in final practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Max Verstappen set the second-fastest time at the Sepang International Circuit, 0.278s off Antonelli's benchmark, with Isack Hadjar third. George Russell could only manage fourth in the other W17.

That comes after Verstappen topped FP1 and both drivers were in the mix during FP2 as well, rounding out a strong Friday for the six-time constructors' champions.

Speaking on Sky Sports F1 commentary after the session, Davidson highlighted how Mercedes' advantage is shrinking quickly, and how the RB22 is emerging as the closest competitor.

Red Bull's form continues from where the team left off in Baku, where Verstappen finished just 0.196s behind race winner Russell, with Hadjar completing a double podium for the Milton Keynes-based squad in third.

And the four-time F1 drivers' champion has finished on the rostrum in the last six grands prix he has completed, with just his retirements at Silverstone and Zandvoort bucking that trend.

"Red Bull would have hoped to be closer to the Mercedes, but they are there or thereabouts once again," Davidson said. "They're quickly becoming the team that's the biggest threat to Mercedes on any given weekend."

Mekies and Verstappen targeting victories

Red Bull sits fourth in the constructors' standings and is the only top-four outfit yet to triumph this season, with Ferrari and then McLaren looking to be the closest rivals to Mercedes.

However, Davidson has tapped into the shifting sands of the competitive order and team principal Laurent Mekies has repeatedly stressed that Red Bull's target for the rest of the campaign is to fight for grand prix wins on merit, rather than rely on others' misfortune.

The Frenchman has pointed to the scale of the RB22's in-season development when reflecting on progress made since the early rounds.

"There is a definitive step forward. We left Japan 1.2 seconds away from pole, China 1.0 seconds away from pole," Mekies said.

"Competition was not going to wait for us with their updates. Everybody has updated the car, but certainly we knew that on top of the development race, we had to solve some of our issues, and we knew there was lap time in it."

For Verstappen, the stakes are personal, too. The 29-year-old has yet to win a grand prix in 2026 and is chasing a maiden victory of the campaign to avoid going winless for the first time since his debut season with Toro Rosso in 2015.

"We are scoring quite a few podiums now, but I want to win," he said ahead of the weekend in Sepang.

"That's what I'm here for, and I'm getting close, but I want at least to win one race this year, so I hope we can do it, of course, at some point."

title: McLaren record surprising financial loss despite record £588 million turnover
excerpt:
The McLaren F1 team recorded a surprising financial loss of £17.3 million GBP after tax in 2025 despite a bumper year on and off-track, where it won both championship titles.

Lando Norris guided McLaren to its first championship double since 1998 in 2025 and won the first drivers' title for the team since Lewis Hamilton in 2008, with the team earning turnover of £588.483 million GBP - a rise of £100 million GBP from the 2024 financial year.

This increased turnover is the result of increased commercial revenue from McLaren's vast array of sponsors and the prize money it earned from Formula 1 for its performance in the constructors' championship, as it successfully defended its constructors' crown.

In the official financial declaration to Companies House, a legal requirement for any company trading in the UK, McLaren then recorded cost of sales of £534.332 million in 2025, leaving it with a gross profit of £54.141 million GBP. In 2024, cost of sales was £159.309 million less at £375.023 million GBP, leaving a gross profit of £113.370 million before any expenses were paid.

On the gross profit of £54.141 million in 2025, the team paid expenses of £129.651 million, which, after some additional income was added, left a before-tax loss for the year of £42.758 million, a fall of nearly £91 million GBP from the £48.462 million profit before tax 12 months prior.

After interest was added and deducted, and then tax applied to the loss, it left McLaren with a bottom-line loss figure of £17.360 million GBP, a fall of £71.196 million GBP from the bottom-line profit of £53.836 million GBP in 2024.

However, the team enjoys strong financial reserves with net assets of £45.948 million GBP on the books, down slightly from the £60.212 million GBP in 2024.

Elsewhere, McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown enjoyed a bumper pay packet for the year.

The documents show that the highest-paid director within the company, believed to be Brown, received a base salary of £8.215 million - a rise from £6.126 million in 2024.

It is also described that payments "in relation to the long-term incentive schemes" were made to Brown, totalling £73.682 million GBP - up from £31.077 million GBP in 2024. This total would make Brown one of the highest-paid executives in all of sport.

One reason for the surprising financial loss of McLaren was that it repaid loans after a cash investment during COVID, when the team nearly went bust.

MSP Sports Capital invested in the team in December 2020, co-investing with UBS O'Connor LLC and the Najafi Companies, with UBS O'Connor, investment group Caspian and Ares Capital all investing a total of £179 million.

By September 2025, the loan notes had been fully repaid with the investors acquiring the wider McLaren Group, granting full ownership.

The Bahraini Mumtalakat sovereign wealth fund remains the majority shareholder.
